resources.string: The bar at the bottom with Trips, Travellers and Settings. Automatic slides it away as soon as you open a trip; the arrow at the top left brings you back. Always keeps it on screen everywhere, except over the photo viewer, the big map and the photo book.
System follows the language of your phone. The screen is built again in the new language when you switch.
Photos you look at are kept on this phone, so you see them again at once and without internet. Once the cache reaches the limit, the photos you have not looked at for longest go first.
Saved photos are cleared. They are fetched again as soon as you are online. Nothing from your trips is lost.
Version %1$s is available. The card on the Trips page installs it.
You are up to date. Build %1$s is the latest.
This build does not look for updates.
On: every change stays on the phone and is never sent.
Off: changes go to the server. Start the app with --ez dryRun true to switch it on.
The real screens, as a new user sees them. A preview changes nothing and sends nothing.
Looks at %1$s for %2$s. This app is build %3$s.
The preview runs the whole card on the Trips page without downloading or installing anything.
The waiting changes are thrown away and never sent.
When, the path and what the server said. Never a token, a password or what was sent.
Hides this page again. Tap the version in About five times to get it back.
No connection to the server. You see saved data; changes wait on this phone.

Looks in your gallery for photos of these trip days and puts them in your timeline and on the map, without uploading them. They then only exist on this phone: companions do not see them, they are not in a share link, and on a new phone they are gone. The photos themselves stay in your gallery.
From your gallery, without sending them to the server.
The photos themselves stay in your gallery. They only disappear from this trip.
No new photos found for these days.
The app may not read your gallery. Allow it under Settings, Apps, MarkMySteps, Permissions.
Places in photos were refused, so they will not appear on the map.
This trip has no dates yet.

resources.string: Ask for an account on your own server. The admin lets you in.
Friends use this to add you to trips. 3 to 30 letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore.
That is not an email address.
Username: 3 to 30 letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore.
That email address or username is already taken.
Too many people are waiting for approval on this server. Try again later.
Too many attempts. Try again in an hour.
Preview: nothing was sent and no account was made.
Your request is with the admin of this server. As soon as they let you in, the app opens by itself.
You can close the app. If it is open or in the background, you get a notification.
You can start using MarkMySteps now.
The admin of this server has turned down your request. Get in touch with them if you think that is a mistake.
Everything stays on your phone. No account, no server, nothing leaves it.
Your location is kept on your phone, even without internet. The tracker runs entirely on your phone.
Stops, nights and transport. Everything adds up as usual.
Photos on your phone are linked to a trip by date and put on the map with their GPS.
The maps and the globe get their tiles straight from OpenStreetMap. No account needed.
Working on one trip together and seeing each other\'s live position.
A private link for the folks at home needs a server to live on.
Everything is on your phone. Make a backup now and then in Settings.
If you keep your photos on your own Immich server, you can connect it later.
A server is just a computer that is always on: an old laptop with Linux and Docker, a Raspberry Pi or a NAS. Install MarkMySteps on it, make an account there and sign in to it in this app.
Without a server: everything stays on this phone.
Follow your route, plan your trip and look back on it later. Everything stays yours.
Without a server there is no account and no password. Your name only appears on your own trips, and stays on this phone.
All your trips as colourful routes on a globe, with a dot for every stop. Tap a trip to open it with your timeline and photos.
Build your route with stops, nights and transport: car, train, boat, or a flight with layovers. The distances and your days add up by themselves.
Every trip keeps its map, its days and its numbers. Your photos land on the right day and in the right place by themselves.
Share with the folks at home
One private link with your map, your days and your photos. Read only, and nobody needs to create an account.
Tracking goes easy on your battery and works without internet: everything is buffered and uploaded later.
Pick your theme. You can always change it later in Settings.
Which airports do you usually fly from? You can change this later in Settings, Preferences.
Denied. You can turn this on later in Settings.
To track your route, the app asks for your location. A GPS point is only saved when you move, which saves your battery.

Without a server, your photos come from your phone\'s gallery. They stay where they are: the app only reads them, and nothing leaves your phone. Android only shares the place in a photo with a separate permission; without it they do not appear on the map.
Only what you need to know: the status of your tracking and updates from your travel companions. No ads, no tips, no reminders to open the app.
Fill in a name and your dates, and add your stops. The rest fills itself in while you travel: your route, your photos and your days.
